# Effect: frequency_shifter

Frequency shifter: shifts every frequency by a fixed number of Hz (unlike pitch shifting, the harmonic relationships are broken).

**Where to put it**: Small shifts (1-10 Hz) give slow phase rotation and widening; large shifts give inharmonic effects; add feedback for rising/falling spiral tones.

Latest parameters: `muser effects frequency_shifter` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shift_hz` | 10 | -2000 – 2000 Hz | Shift amount. +/-1-10 subtle rotation; above +/-50 obviously detuned |
| `feedback` | 0 | 0 – 0.95 | Feedback. Higher sounds more like an endless rising/falling spiral (Shepard tone) |
| `mix` | 1 | 0 – 1 | Dry/wet mix. At 0.5 a small shift sounds like a phaser |

All parameters can be omitted and take their default when omitted; when a value is out of range, `muser validate` reports the exact location.

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "frequency_shifter", "shift_hz": 4, "mix": 0.5 }
```

## Scenario presets

- Subtle rotation, widening (like a phaser)

  ```json
  {"type": "frequency_shifter", "shift_hz": 3, "mix": 0.5}
  ```

- Dissonant detuned effect

  ```json
  {"type": "frequency_shifter", "shift_hz": 120, "mix": 0.7}
  ```

- Endlessly rising spiral (Barber-pole)

  ```json
  {"type": "frequency_shifter", "shift_hz": 8, "feedback": 0.8, "mix": 0.6}
  ```

## Tips and common mistakes

- Unlike pitch shifting: after frequency shifting the overtones are no longer integer multiples, so a large shift is always dissonant.
- A small shift (1-10 Hz) + mix 0.5 is most common: it rotates slowly without going out of tune.
- With very high feedback it builds up for a long time, so leave time for the tail (`--tail` when rendering).
